utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we hear the witness, I have an announcement to make. The Bench would like to revoke the rulings we made yesterday concerning of the scheduling. Yesterday afternoon I received a notice that the extraordinary Plenary is cancelled, so on Friday morning we'll return to the normal scheduling. Thank you. Are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise at this stage? Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Pardon me, Your Honour. I'm sorry about that. Your Honours, it was indicated to me last night by my learned colleague Mr. Weiner that due to scheduling issues that the Prosecution have, they would like to move the witness Eminovic forward. The plan was, I think, that Mr. Salihamidzic come and then Mr. Eminovic. But because of personal reasons for that witness, Mr. Eminovic, the Prosecution want to bring him forward. Can I indicate that we are happy to accommodate that but that the one difficulty it's going to cause us is in compiling our -- our list of documents that we have to put to that witness. It may be that there's a delay in relation to that, and I apologise for that delay in advance. But we'll do everything we can to accommodate, and we think the Prosecution have given us good reasons why they need to move him forward so that we'll -- we'll go along with that. Could I just indicate there'll be a short -- a bit of a delay in terms of giving them the list of -- and providing that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that if there's any change of the witness order, the party who is doing that should inform the other party as early as possible so that to let the other party be prepared for the case. Thank you. Well, could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down, please. Did you have a good rest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Sachdeva: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kadic.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to take you back very briefly to when you told the Court about being billeted in this house in Grabovica. Can you tell the Court how many people were in that house with you.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 30 or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they from your company, in the 2nd Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you told us that you saw Celo and his soldiers at a line-up the day after you arrived, and then you described that there was intermittent shooting that day. I want you now to cast your mind back to that evening, and if you can, tell me whether your soldiers spoke to Celo's soldiers, if they did at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, just a short objection about the timing of the line-up. I'm not sure that the witness indeed indicated that the line-up would have taken place the day after he arrived. I think that's a matter that should be clarified with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We heard some evidence about the line-up, but I'm not sure, you know, which one it is. And maybe you could ask some questions about the time to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm ask the witness to clarify, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That line-up we spoke about, when did it occur, in relation to your arrival?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived on that day after noon. On the following day, Celo's men came and the line-up was the following morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day of the line-up, in the evening, did your soldiers speak to Celo's soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not have any contacts with that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in that evening of -- of the day of the line-up, what were your soldiers doing?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were told not to go away from the houses, not to go far from the houses, to stay close to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your soldiers and yourself were in and around your house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that evening, what did your soldiers do in the house?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have anything to eat that evening?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had packed lunches, and we also received the meat that the army prepared for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you eat your packed lunches and the meat in the evening of that -- that day, the day of the line-up?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the soldiers were sitting in the meadow across from the house on that evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly what time was that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 9.00 in the evening maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when your soldiers were sitting there in the meadow, were you there as well?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. I was in the house where we were billeted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who your soldiers were speaking to?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few soldiers from Celo's unit dropped by, that told them that they would be shooting a little and that they shouldn't pay attention to that because they had nothing to do with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how did you know about this conversation?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the following morning, Zdenko Jelisic told me that. He was one of those lads sitting on the grass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was Zdenko Jelisic staying?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the same house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move to the following morning. That morning, did you go anywhere outside of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that morning, we went to the house where our command and commander were. We were lined up because the previous evening we were told that we were supposed to go to Dreznica, where an action was supposed to start.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you lined up in the morning?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the house where the commander was billeted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what time was that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7.00 in the morning, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after that meeting with the commander, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the old road leading up to the tunnel, at the exit out of Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as I said, I'm going to show you a photograph soon and I'll ask you to point out that road for the benefit of the Court. But while you were travelling along that road, did you see anything in particular?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw a dead woman on the road. Two days before that, we had spoken to her. We were billeted in her house, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the dead woman wearing?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that she had a short-sleeved dress on. I can't remember any details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how far were you from her when you saw her?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not more than two metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to establish or -- well, were you able to establish how she was killed?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the road, there were pieces of her head. I couldn't see any other injuries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any weapons in and around her?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as you carried on that road, did you see anything else?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little bit lower, there was another body, but it was not on the road. It was some 15 metres away from the road, by the lake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this body of a man or a woman?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly how old was this man? If you can decipher.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We couldn't see how old he was. His face was facing the water, so it's hard for me to say how old he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, were you able to see what kind of clothes he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ordinary work clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you say "ordinary work clothes," do you mean civilian or military clothes?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian. Civilian work clothes. A pair of trousers, a jacket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the lady and the man that you've just spoken about, did you know of any other civilians that were killed in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miroslav Masal told me about another civilian who had been killed when we were in the tunnel. As we passed those two dead bodies, we spent the whole day and the whole night in the tunnel. And when we were talking about what had happened, Masal told me that he had seen another civilian across the road from the house where we were previously lined up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was staying in that house where you were lined up?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 2nd Battalion was there in that house. I remember that Adnan Solakovic and Samir Pezo, his brother-in-law, were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Miroslav Masal tell you about this civilian that he saw?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After we saw the killed civilians, we talked to each other about what had happened. Everybody saw these two killed civilians. We passed by them. And then he said that he saw another one, a taller one, who was in the shrubs or in the bushes, so that not everybody could see that civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you how he knew this -- this body was of a civilian?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a man wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You told us that you stayed in the tunnel. Where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were supposed to go to Dreznica, from the tunnel along the old road to Dreznica. Since that road was under the constant HVO shelling, we could not take that road. We had to climb the mountain and cross it in order to get to Dreznica. In any case, we did arrive in Dreznica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We returned to Grabovica two days and one night later, having spent two nights -- two days and one night on that mountain that I can't remember the name of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after your return to Grabovica, where did you go, if you went anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We returned to Grabovica during the night. There were lorries waiting for us there. We got onto the lorries and went to Zuka's base. And after that, to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, I'd like to show the witness -- I think it's -- P4, photograph P4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kadic, can you see the photograph on your screen?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Grabovica village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the place where you and your fellow soldiers were staying?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to it, please.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the house, here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You've circled that house. Can you -- can you draw the figure number "1" just by it, please.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And similarly, can you circle the house where Adnan Solakovic was staying and put the figure number "2" there.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you see the place where you saw Celo and his soldiers at the line-up? Well, firstly, do you see that place there?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you also circle that and put the number "3" there, please.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you can, I'd like you to with a dotted line just mark the route that you took that morning on your way to Dreznica.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just go a bit further, please. If you'd just take the dotted line further, or put an arrow at the end.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you can, can you circle the area where you saw the dead woman on your way to Dreznica.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you place a figure "4" there, please.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you do the same for the man that you saw in the water.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you place a figure "5" above the circle.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Your Honours. I'd like to tender that into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I guess there's no objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number is 265.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross? Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Good morning, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Mettraux:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, witness. My name is Guenael Mettraux. I'm co-counsel for Sefer Halilovic. I'd like to ask you a few general questions to start with about the 2nd Independent Battalion. Prior to your being sent to Herzegovina, the 2nd Independent Battalion had not been assigned a particular part of the front line to defend around Sarajevo. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 2nd Independent in fact operated more as a light and mobile battalion which would be sent to various parts of the front line where there was a need for reinforcement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from July 1993 onwards, the 2nd Independent Battalion was also sent to perform military operations outside of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And part of the 2nd Independent Battalion was sent, for instance, to Igman, Bjelasnica or, in November 1993, to Bradina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In all of those assignments, the 2nd Independent performed very well and acquired a reputation as a good fighting unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the summer and the autumn of 1993, the Independent -- 2nd Independent Battalion consisted of approximately 200 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've indicated that the commander of that battalion was a person named Adnan Solakovic.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was known as a brave fighter and he was respected and obeyed by his men; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was his habit as a commander to take part in military operations together with his men?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not always.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he did in the case of the operation in Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was on the ground in Herzegovina, but he was in the command throughout this time. He did not go into action with his men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as the reputation of the battalion was concerned, as you pointed out earlier, it had a good reputation and it was not known in any way as a criminal battalion, or it did not have a criminal reputation.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday in your evidence in chief you indicated to the Prosecutor that Mr. Solakovic was the commander of the 2nd Independent Battalion and that this battalion was in turn a part of the 1st Corps, which in turn was commanded by a person named Vahid Karavelic; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also indicated yesterday that you didn't know who had deployed the 2nd Independent Battalion but you indicated to the Prosecution that you were told to go to Herzegovina by your commander, Senad Sakovic, when he returned from a meeting - and I quote - "with the commander"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the commander which you were referring to was the commander of the 1st Corps, Mr. Vahid Karavelic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who attended the meeting after which our commander transmitted the order to us. All I know is that Senad Sakovic transmitted this order to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know, sir, who gave that order to Senad Sakovic; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not all members of the 2nd Independent Battalion were sent to Herzegovina, sir. Only about 100 or 120 of them were sent; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is your battalion commander, Adnan Solakovic, who decided which soldier would go and that choice would in turn be forwarded to you by your platoon commander, Mr. Sakovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like now to take you to another part of your evidence which you've given earlier to the Prosecution. You understood as you arrived in Herzegovina that your battalion was to be resubordinated to Zuka's unit or Zulfikar's unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that at the time. Later on I learned that we were supposed to be resubordinated and be commanded by Zulfikar, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your commander, Adnan Solakovic, resisted the resubordination to Zuka's; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a result of his resisting this resubordination, you were actually not resubordinated to Zuka's unit and remained independent; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also explained that you stopped at Zuka's base on your arrival in Jablanica. As you arrived, you were greeted by men from Zuka's unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the first time that you were informed that you would stay in the village of Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A number of -- a number of members of Zuka's unit accompanied you to the village of Grabovica as you went there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as you arrived in Grabovica, you were told that three houses had been provided for your accommodation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived in Grabovica, our commander told us what house we were to be billeted in, where the 3rd Company was to be billeted. That's what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you referred to "our commander," you referred to Mr. Sakovic, your platoon commander; is that correct -- or company commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Senad Sakovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was not for you to go and look for a house. He told you what house you were supposed to billet yourself in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if I've understood your evidence properly in chief, there were in fact three different houses in which members of the 2nd Independent Battalion were billeted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the first house -- that could be the first house at the entrance of the village which you've indicated Adnan Solakovic had been billeted; is that correct

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And other officers of the 2nd Independent Battalion had been accommodated with him.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You already indicated that Samir Pezo stayed in the same house as Adnan Solakovic, but there were other individuals, such as Jasmin Panjeta; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His nickname was -- or rather, he had a nickname, so I didn't really know that that was his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was his nickname Pike?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, Pike.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Pike in the same house as Adnan Solakovic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was. I can't be certain, but I think he was. Pike was always at the command, so it would have been logical for him to be billeted there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it would have been logical as well for Zakir Okovic to be billeted in that house?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zakir Okovic? Yes, it would have been logical, but he went to do reconnaissance, so to what extent he was present there, I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Haris Svrakic, also known as Pilot? Was he in that house?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, sir, there was a second house in which you resided. And you've indicated with a number "1" on the picture that was shown to you by the Prosecution. You've indicated yesterday that as you arrived, the house was empty of its owners; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also indicated that on the day when you arrived, you meet -- sorry, you met the owner of that house and had a conversation with her; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That person did not suggest, did she, that she had somehow been expelled from her house or that she was otherwise unhappy of having left that house?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. All she told us was that that was her house and that she was temporarily staying in another house with some other people. That's all she told us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And she also told you that the furniture which had been in her house had been taken by soldiers, didn't she?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But she didn't tell you, did she, when those furnitures had been taken by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've indicated, I believe, that around 30 soldiers from the 2nd Independent Battalion stayed together with you in that house. And I would like to ask you to think back. And I will ask you -- I will put to you the name of a number of people, and I'd like you to tell me whether those people were or were not with you in that house at the time. Sakovic Senad, was he in that house with you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Mustafa Mujo Karic? Was he with you in that house?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Jelisic Zdenko? Was he in that house, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Miroslav Masal? Was he in that house with you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Ivisic Zvonko?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Gobelic Dzevad?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zoran Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, sir, if I'm correct, there was a third house in the village where members of the 2nd Independent Battalion were staying; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the reply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you repeat your answer. The interpreter could not pick it up.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Prosecution Exhibit number 4, P4 again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you need the original picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But not -- yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you see that third house on the picture which you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please circle it with the pen, number "1" next to it.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you see on the right-hand side from the house in which you were staying, a rather smallish white or grey house without a roof? Can you see that house, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, yes, it doesn't have a roof on this picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it didn't have a roof at the time either, sir; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember, sir, whether anyone was living in that house at the time of the events in the village of Grabovica? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no one lived there; or no, you can't remember?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember seeing people entering or getting out of the house at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, people left their houses very seldom, at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Am I correct, sir, in --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: First I would like perhaps to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there's no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's document 266.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is that correct -- am I correct in suggesting to you that you remained in the village of Grabovica at all times; that is, from the moment when you arrived in Grabovica until the time you left for combat?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you did not go to Jablanica at any time or did you otherwise get out of the village during that period.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At all times, you stayed in the -- in your house most of the time and infrequently you would go on the balcony of that house or in front of the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In front of the house, there was a plateau, and that's where we sat most of the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also given evidence yesterday to this Trial Chamber that as you arrived, the atmosphere in the village was peaceful; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was no conflict with the locals and, in fact, they received you well.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was no indication at that time that anything bad would happen in the village.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've indicated, sir, that the day after you arrived in Grabovica, members of Celo's unit arrived in the village as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the only unit that arrived in the village on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And aside from the 2nd Independent Battalion and Celo's unit, there were no other units from Sarajevo billeted in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were aware of the fact that Caco's soldiers had been billeted in Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew that they had arrived, but we didn't know where they were billeted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Yesterday you've indicated in your evidence in chief that Celo's unit was one of those units - and I quote your words - "that could not be placed under the army command." Now, I have a question about that, sir: In giving that evidence yesterday, were you in fact or in substance reiterating a comment that you made to the Prosecution during your proofing session of last week where you said that Celo's unit - and again I quote - "had a reputation of not obeying orders"? Is that what you were telling the Trial Chamber yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what you were in fact suggesting or stating was that some members of this unit apparently considered that they could decide at times whether to obey or not to obey orders which came from outside the brigade. Is that so, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But despite this apparent lack of discipline, Celo's unit was known as a good and strong fighting unit in Sarajevo. They were much admired, in fact, by many of the inhabitants of Sarajevo at the time.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also indicated, sir, in your evidence yesterday that there were a number of refugees in the village of Grabovica at the time when you came to the village, and you've also indicated to this Trial Chamber that you met one of those refugees, an old man who had been a judge in Sarajevo. Can you remember that evidence, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell this Trial Chamber what this old man told you as you met him in the village.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came to us. He asked us where we were from, what unit. And he told us that he was from Mostar and that before the war, he had worked as a judge in Sarajevo, that he had been imprisoned in the Dretelj camp, that he had been exchanged, and that he was accommodated on the left bank of the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the Dretelj camp, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A camp where the HVO army imprisoned Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that old man tell you what happened to him in that camp as he was detained?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told us that he had been maltreated and tortured in various ways.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were other refugees or former camp inmates -- sorry, I'll -- I'll withdraw that question. Did you meet any other refugees during the time or former camp inmates during the time when you were in the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any of them?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none except the man we talked to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is another issue, sir, that I would like to discuss with you. As you arrived in the village of Grabovica, as you described it, there was no checkpoint at the entrance of the village, was there?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were on trucks. I didn't see any checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what you know for certain, sir, is that one was set up after members of Celo's unit had arrived in the village; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There had been a meeting between the commanding officers of the 2nd Independent Battalion and Celo's unit when it was decided that such a checkpoint should be set up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's what Senad Sakovic told you when he came back from that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that checkpoint, sir, was manned by two men at all times: One from the 2nd Independent Battalion and one from the 9th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as you could tell, it was not reinforced at any stage during your stay in the village.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see or hear about anyone being prevented from entering the village at that time.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this morning you recounted an incident which was reported to you by, I believe, Zvonko Ivisic about other soldiers coming to your soldiers or to members of the 2nd Independent Battalion and telling them that there would be a little shooting and that they shouldn't worry so much about it. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just a minor objection, Your Honour. I think the name of the person who told the witness is -- isn't correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, it's -- I thank the Prosecution. I think it's Zdenko Jelisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Jelisic give you the name -- the names or nicknames of those three -- two or three individuals that came to this group of soldiers? Did he know them?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he describe them to you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't describe them to me either. He simply said that they were from Celo's unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thereafter, sir, you in fact heard the sound of shooting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't tell me that -- when the shooting started afterwards, he told me that they had come. But as for the shooting, there was sporadic shooting all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And such sporadic shooting, sir, was not unusual, was it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, sir, because of the rising tension in the village, a number of non-Bosniak members of the 2nd Independent Battalion were taken to Solakovic's house; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were Croats and Serbs in this house too, but it was said that they should not be called by name and that they should not be given guard duty, that they should be given nicknames.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those Serbs and Croats in fact stayed in your house.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were some in my house. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was no line-up at that point where Adnan Solakovic told you what was happening in the village and gave you orders or gave you weapons at that stage, was there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no line-up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a short matter of timing. You've indicated, I believe, that the 9th or the -- Celo's unit arrived the day after you had arrived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that it is the day after they had arrived that you saw Celo coming back in the village and organising a line-up of 20 or 30 men; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you left for Dreznica on that same day, sir; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I think the evidence was that they left for Dreznica the next -- the following day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we lost the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you leave the village on that very same day or was it the next day that you left for the village?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the morning of the following day that we left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was -- were weapons taken from you at any stage during your stay in the village of Grabovica, or did you keep your weapons with you at all stages?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you kept them at all times.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the morning, I think you've indicated at around 7.00 a.m., on the morning when you left, Adnan Solakovic lined you up and told you about leaving for combat. That was the only line-up, as far as you can tell and as far as you could see, the only line-up organised by Adnan Solakovic during that period. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all of you -- all members of the 2nd Independent Battalion left on that occasion. No one was left behind in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the men remained in Grabovica. I don't know how many. Some did. Some stayed back. Very few men stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, during your stay in Grabovica, you never saw Vehbija Karic, did you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nor, as a matter of fact, did you see Caco, Zuka, or Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody but the two of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And no member of your battalion told you at the time that they had seen Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the time, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No one came back in the house from the balcony or from outside telling you, "Hey, I've just seen Sefer Halilovic passing by." That didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I -- I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's a fact, sir, that you told the Prosecutor investigator, Mr. Nikolai Mikhailov, when he interviewed you. You said, "I didn't see Sefer Halilovic in the village and no one else in my battalion told me that he had seen Sefer Halilovic"; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you were in the -- in the village at the time. And you've indicated that you saw a number of dead bodies at the time but that you spent most of the time in your houses. Would it be possible, according to you, that refugees might have taken part in the killing in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: It's a speculative question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's a speculative question, and the witness also testified that he did not know there were refugees in that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will -- I will reformulate it then. The question was poorly put.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After having discussed with members of your battalion, did you hear or did anyone from your battalion suggest that refugees might have taken part in the killing?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the crimes that were committed in Grabovica at the time, they had nothing to do with the operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, it had nothing to do with what you personally or your battalion were fighting for; namely, a multi-ethnic Bosnia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, that was totally contrary to what you were fighting for and believing in.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is still difficult to understand for you how one part of the Bosnian army would have to protect some of its members from another part of the Bosnian army; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've indicated, I believe, that after two or three days in combat you were ordered back to Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you came back to Grabovica, all of the bodies or at least the bodies that you had seen had disappeared from the village; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We came back during the night, so I can't say whether they had been removed or whether they were still there. It was dark. I couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't see any bodies, did you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were no other troops present in the village at the time.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, I would like to ask you a short number of questions about what happened in October 1993. In -- at the end of October 1993, there was a big operation in which many of those involved in the Grabovica operation were arrested. That operation came to be known as Trebevic. Do you know about that operation, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know about it from hearing it from the press, isn't that correct, from the media.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the media, yes. And also, we were at the base at the time and we were told that we had to maintain the state of combat readiness because this was happening in the town, that there was a showdown with those units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you, sir, were not arrested during that operation.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody from our unit was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you've anticipated my last two questions, and I thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be our questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-exam?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just -- just one, Your Honour, one question. Re-examined by Mr. Sachdeva:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kadic, in response to counsel for the Defence, you told him that the non-Bosniak members of your unit were given nicknames. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were they given nicknames?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For their -- their personal safety.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why were they in danger?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what we were told at the time, that we shouldn't call them by their real names, that they should be given nicknames. If something should happen, it was not advisable at the time to call them by some other names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what -- what could happen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, it's a tiny bit speculative, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I don't -- I think there's one step further from the previous question. This question is allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. What could happen?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that, but I suppose that the command or the commanders held a meeting and that's what they decided. We were forbidden to move around and to socialise with that unit that had arrived, and that's why they told us not to call these people by their own names, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say that they were given these nicknames for their personal safety, who could have jeopardised their personal safety?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably some people from that unit that arrived at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Celo's unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge El Mahdi. JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. Questioned by the Court: JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Witness, I'd like to clarify one point. Actually, your answer to a question that was put to you. The question was - and I'll quote in English - [In English] Did you see Caco, Zuka, or Sefer Halilovic - [No interpretation] - [In English] No, nobody but the two of them. [Interpretation] Do you remember that answer?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I saw Adnan Solakovic and Ramiz Delalic, and that's who I meant. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So the two that you saw were who?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adnan Solakovic and Ramiz Delalic. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you. And I have another question for you, sir. This question is relative to when you said that you kept your weapons while you were billeted in the house that you showed to us in the photo. Did all the soldiers that were with you keep their weapons as well?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all the soldiers. However, once we were billeted in the house, the weapons were in the house. And as people left the house, nobody took any arms with them. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. But you kept the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Did you have ammunition as well?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA KADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you. [In English] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge's question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I think our channel got confused. [French interpretation on the English Channel)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this point, are there any other questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. We wish you a very pleasant journey back home. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are we continuing with the next witness, or are we going to have a break? And are there any submissions from the Prosecution concerning this next witness? Any protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: None, Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The only submission from the Defence would be that a break would be welcomed at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh, thank you very much. So we'll take a break, and we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Chana, are you ready for your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour. There's one matter I would like to raise before the witness comes in, and that would be that in respect of those documents, Your Honour, that I was supposed to tell you the one that the Defence tendered through Jusuf Jasarevic, the Defence has no objections to the ones which were tendered by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, are you saying on behalf on the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I mean, sorry, the Prosecution has no objection. Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: They're Defence documents

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: The next witness can now be called in, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So the next witness is 89(F).

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: It's 89(F) yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning once again, Your Honour. No, there is no objection on the part of the Defence as to this witness being 89(F)'d as it goes. But this is simply a number of matters which we would like to put on the record in relation to this. The first one is that the Prosecution is going to seek to tender a new statement, as it goes, of this witness which was taken recently, and we're very grateful to the Prosecution for giving it to us in a very timely fashion, Your Honour. There is simply one issue: We believe that where a new statement of a witness is taken and signed by that witness and then tendered pursuant to that Rule, it would fall under Rule 66(A), in terms of disclosure, which means in turn that such a statement would have to be provided in a language which the accused understands. We've informed Mr. Halilovic about the content of this statement, and he has waived his right to receive a translation of that document in B/C/S, but we would be grateful to the Prosecution if they intend to tender such a document again in the future to provide us as well with a B/C/S translation. There is a second matter which we would like to raise in relation to this, and this is a concern which Your Honour has raised in the past, and the Defence notes that the Prosecution has asked for protective measures on no less than six occasions and has asked to tender its evidence in chief pursuant to 89(F) on three occasions. It was granted on two. The Defence mentioned that fact because it is quite concerned about the rights of Mr. Halilovic and the public interest that there is in a public trial, and we think that Mr. Halilovic's right to -- to a public trial should be guaranteed and that those applications should be limited to the absolutely necessary. Finally -- or not finally, as a matter of fact, but further, the Defence would like to point out that evidence which is tendered in written form as opposed to being given orally in court should be given less weight, as it goes, than evidence which would have been given orally. The final point that we would like to raise is this: It is the Defence submission that where the Prosecution has decided to tender its evidence in chief in written form through a statement, the Rules on re-examination should be interpreted particularly strictly in such a context and the Defence should not be permitted to achieve in re-examination what it declined to do in chief. And that would be all of our submissions in that respect and -- I meant the Prosecutor. I'm suffering from the same failure or failing as my colleague from the other side. I meant that the Prosecution should not be permitted to do so. And I'm grateful. And as I pointed out earlier, we have no objection to this particular witness being heard pursuant to 89(F).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. And just one thing to clarify: You said that there is a new statement which fell into the scope of the Rule 66(A). But to my understanding, it is not a new statement. It's just a summary of all the previous statements into one document. So I wonder whether this kind of practice -- I mean, the summary, falls into the Rule 66(A).

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we -- we are in your hands in that regard, Your Honour. We believe that this is a new statement, insofar as it is not only a summary of the witness's evidence, insofar as the source is mentioned in that documents are concerned. There are a number of issues and a number of facts which have been left out by the Prosecution. Your Honour is quite right to point out that some of the paragraphs in that document are merely what would appear to be cut and pasted from other statements, and we have no problem with that. But to the extent that the evidence would vary - and it has at least in one relatively important respect - or to the extent that a number of facts or matters are being left out by the party tendering that document, we would submit that this would constitute a new statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think, you know, it's purely a theoretical issue and we'll deal with it at a later stage. But now we have the witness waiting outside. Could we have the witness now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Chana:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Saban. Could you please give us your full name.

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Saban Neziric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neziric, I would like to show you a statement. Would you please look at it and indicate to Your Honours whether that is your signature on each page of this particular statement.

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this read out to you in a language that you understood?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you confirm the contents of the statement and the veracity?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And Madam Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number will be 267.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will give a short summary of what evidence this witness testifies about. Your Honours, his name is Saban Neziric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in November 1992, you started to work in the security of the hydroelectric plant in Grabovica as a guard.

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... building was situated on the left side of the Neretva River, and you could see the right part of the village of Grabovica which had Croat residents. In autumn, some troops from Sarajevo arrived and they were billeted on the right side of the Neretva River in Grabovica. Sometime in September, you were on duty guarding the office building on the left side of the Neretva River and heard sounds of shooting coming from the right side of the village. The shooting continued for some time and Zuka, which is Alispago Zulfikar, was called to inform him about the shooting and for him to take some action. After ten minutes of this call, Zuka's car came to the right side of the Neretva. When Zuka's car was in Grabovica on the right side of the Neretva, the shooting stopped. When Zuka's car left -- Sorry, Your Honour. When Zuka's car left, the shooting stopped at that time. The same day, you went to visit the village and learned that some civilians in Grabovica on both sides of the river had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, to interrupt. I think the transcript suggests that when Zuka's car left, the shooting stopped. I understand from the witness statement that that's when the shooting started.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, Your Honour. It was obviously a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: -- typo in my thing. Yes, can I correct that for the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Zuka's car was in Grabovica, the shooting stopped and when Zuka's car left, the shooting started. I'm obliged to learned counsel for pointing it out. The same day the witness entered the village and learned that some civilians in Grabovica on both sides of the river had been killed. You also on the left side of the Neretva River saw a dead body of a male. Some days later, you witnessed the same corpse burnt and this time noticed a hole at the back of his head. You also found a body buried in the ground. Sometime later you saw human -- a human hand appearing from the ground. On one occasion after the events in Grabovica you entered the toilet of a new railway station and noticed three human skulls in that toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's not exactly an objection, but the Defence would just like to understand what -- what the purpose of this summary is, because we have already been provided with a written summary or what the Prosecution purports to be a written summary of his own evidence, and we're being given a second version of that evidence. So we simply -- we understand or we think we should understand the Prosecution practice as merely being a summary for the -- for the purpose of the Trial Chamber and that the witness will not be asked to adopt what is being read out to him at this stage, and we would just like to clarify this matter at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: This is a short summary from the statement for the record and for the public to know what evidence this particular witness is going to testify about. I've only got one line left and that's the end of my summary, Your Honour. It's exactly from the 89(F) statement, Your Honour, not a thing extra has been add or deleted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that is the normal practice in applying the Rule 89(F). That summary should be very concise and should be very short. You may proceed, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Now, you also will state that you met Zulfikar Alispago before the events in Grabovica and you said -- and Zulfikar Alispago said to you that he wanted to look after the Croats in Grabovica and wanted to send doctors and, in fact, doctors did come on a regular basis to Grabovica. Your Honour, with that, I -- my examination-in-chief is concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Mettraux:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, witness. My name is Guenael Mettraux, and I'm appearing as co-counsel for Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your responsibility, sir, in the office of the hydroelectric plant in Grabovica was to guard the office building, which was on the left side of the village, as well as to patrol the territory around that office; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would work in shifts of two people.

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While one of you would stay in the building, the other one would go around the territory in question. There would always be, in other words, someone in the office building at all times; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Not necessarily. Sometimes we walked together, and at other times it was the way you described.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And could you see, sir, the right side of the village from the office in which you were working, in the building?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: On one side of the building, we were able to see through the windows, but from the whole building we could see the right bank of the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And your shifts, sir, would last 12 hours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 24. And then -- they would start either at 7.00 in the morning or 7.00 in the evening and last until the next day at the same time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: From morning till morning. From 8.00 in the morning, for example, until 8.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during those shifts, sir, you would not always be paired with the same person. What I mean to say is you worked with different people, depending on the time or the occasion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: To start with, we worked in pairs, and later on we were withdrawn to the dam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that one occasion relevant to this Tribunal, you had been paired with a man called Alija Turkic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a few general questions about the village of Grabovica. Since May 1993 when the village had been retaken by the ABiH, the atmosphere in the village was good and stable, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were no problems between the ABiH and local Croats.

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I was able to understand, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And local residents were treated well and with respect, again as far as you could see or tell.

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In particular, one individual, Zulfikar Alispago, known as Zuka, was making sure that the local residents would be treated properly and with dignity; isn't that the case, sir?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was doing his best not only to keep the locals from being harmed in any way, but he was also ensuring their well-being, for instance, by bringing in a doctor every Friday of the week; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: I don't remember what day it was, whether it was Thursday or Friday. I can't say exactly. But a doctor did come every week, yes. Up until this incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't worry about the date, sir. It's been -- it's been many years now. We will not blame you for anything like that. But you knew about those visits by the doctors and the consultations because they took place in the very office in which you were working; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the local Croats were also nice and grateful to Zuka for arranging these facilities for them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: I didn't discuss this with anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you could see that they returned the friendliness to the ABiH people or to people like you who worked in the office building; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also heard Zulfikar Alispago, Zuka, repeating on several occasions that no one should be hurt in that village.

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: He spoke to me and said that no one was to interfere with the Croats or to rob them. That's certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the locals, there were soldiers who had been billeted in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there were a unit called Cedo's Wolves which had been accommodated in the very building in which you worked; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Yes. Initially no, but then later on Cedo's Wolves arrived and that's when there were soldiers in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were no problems between Cedo's Wolves and the local residents at that time.

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then later on in September of 1993, new soldiers arrived in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the right bank of the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, you had been forbidden to go to the right side of the village; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Nobody can forbid me to go. It wasn't forbidden.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't go, sir.

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: Not at that time, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did not meet personally any members from those units.

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: I did come across them, both at a distance and close up, but I just passed by them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not stop to talk to any of them, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: I spoke to one of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he introduce himself to you?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he wearing any insignia, sir?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are not certain what units had been billeted at the time in Grabovica, from -- from your own eyes and your own experience. You only heard about those later. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: At first, I didn't know. And later on, I found out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard, for instance, that Celo's unit had been billeted in that village; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: That was later. I learned that later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it, sir, that you learned that Celo's unit had been billeted in the village?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: I can't say precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you remember, sir, who told you that Celo's unit had been billeted in the village at that time?

utterances.speaker: SABAN NEZIRIC
utterances.text: I can't remember that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would that be the same in relation to Caco's unit, sir?
