This conversation was attended by Edib Saric, who at the time was the commander of a platoon the name of which was the Wolves. Salihamidzic Zijad -- I don't know whether his name was Zijad. There was one person called Salihamidzic in the police radio station. And Sead Brankovic was also a policeman, but we -- whom we had very correct relationship. And I believe that this particular piece of information came from any of these sources, either Brankovic or possibly Salihamidzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next line: "The situation in Grabovica is currently under control, which also comes as a result of the fact that" - and this next part is underlined - "in the wake of these events Ramiz Delalic executed one soldier. New sentence: "You will be informed of any new details." Again, casting your memory back, are you able to tell us now what the source of your information was about the alleged execution of a soldier?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN EMINOVIC
utterances.text: I really wouldn't know. I wouldn't know who the source of this particular piece of information was. I wouldn't be able to answer that, and I don't know whether he was executed or not. As I said a while ago, this was a customary way of communication with the chief of administration when it came to similar things.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Could the witness -- the next document I wish to show the witness is MFI D228.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while that's on the way, Mr. Eminovic, that was a report which you sent to Mr. Jasarevic. What was Mr. Jasarevic's response to receiving that report?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN EMINOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the previous document, the one that I had on the screen? You want to know what his response was to that document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: NERMIN EMINOVIC
utterances.text: The response was a request for new information. And you can see it in the following document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's -- to be quite clear, it's MFI D228, which is a document dated the 18th of September, 1993 addressed to the 6th Corps command chief of military security service. And you told us earlier that was you. Did you receive that document?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN EMINOVIC
utterances.text: I did. I suppose I did. I can't remember every document. However, it was addressed to me. I must have -- I must have received it. There's no reason why I shouldn't have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the order says: "In order to brief the Presidency of the republic and the Supreme Command Staff of the army, please forward a report on the killing of the civilian population in the villages of Uzdol and Kriz, Prozor municipality, and Grabovica -- municipality, Jablanica municipality. The report should include the place and time of the event, the establishment of the unit that took part in the event," and so on. Now, just leaving out Uzdol for the moment and concentrating on Grabovica, what was your response to receiving this particular follow-up order from the chief of the military security service?

utterances.speaker: NERMIN EMINOVIC
utterances.text: The previous report -- when General Jasarevic sent this request, he did not have the previous report in his hands. And my response to this was as follows: I made an attempt to communicate as the information that is requested with regard to Uzdol and Kriz in the municipality of Prozor, and I tried to establish communication with them but I encountered a lot of problems there. Mr. Jasarevic urged us on several occasions to send the report to him. In any case, my response was that I had partly met the request as per the previous document and that we were trying to get in touch with the independent battalion in Prozor in order to get more information. To be honest, this was the first time that I ever learnt of anything that might have happened in Uzdol. Before that, I never knew that anything happened in Uzdol in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time today, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Now the hearing for today is adjourned, and we'll meet tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 11th day of March, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
